html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. MSK: Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka; CRM: customer relationship management; NAS: network-attached storage; IAM: Identity and Access Management; VPC: Virtual Private Cloud; ORC: Optimized Row Columnar; ETL: extract, transform, load; AZ: Availability Zone; EMR: Elastic MapReduce; LF: Lake Formation; KMS: Key Management Service; TLS: Transport Layer Security; NFS: Network File System; SMB: Server Message Block; HDFS: Hadoop Distributed File System; EFS: Elastic File System; SQS: Simple Queue Service; EC2: Elastic Compute Cloud

  • Choose an ingestion pattern by frequency, size and speed
  • Design streaming pipelines with Kinesis, Firehose, Flink and MSK
  • Transform data and convert formats with Glue
  • Build and secure a data lake with S3, Glue and Lake Formation
  • Query and visualize with Athena, OpenSearch and Quick, and transfer data with DataSync

2Ingestion patterns, streaming, Glue and the data lake

Running case

Lantern and Loom Learns from Its Data

  • Clickstream events pour in all day
  • Order exports arrive each night as CSV files
  • CRM data sits in a SaaS application, and warehouse files on an on-premises NAS
  • Analysts want SQL on S3 and dashboards, with customer columns restricted
  • Your job: choose the ingestion, transformation, security and analytics services

Data Ingestion Patterns

Pattern When Typical services
Streaming Events continuously, results in seconds Kinesis Data Streams, MSK, Firehose
Near real time Deliver to a store in minutes Data Firehose
Batch Files on a schedule: hourly, nightly S3 uploads, Glue jobs, DataSync
SaaS and partner Data in applications or from third parties AppFlow, Data Exchange
  • Size for volume (MB/s), record size, frequency and number of consumers
  • Secure each access point: IAM, VPC endpoints, encryption
Exam tip

Seconds mean streaming; hours mean batch; the word managed pipeline means Firehose.

Amazon Kinesis Data Streams

  • Collects and processes large streams of records in real time; a record is usually readable in under a second
  • A stream is made of shards: about 1 MB/s or 1,000 records/s written and 2 MB/s read per shard
  • On-demand mode scales automatically; provisioned mode needs a shard count you set
  • Several consumers can read the same stream independently; enhanced fan-out gives each its own throughput
  • Order is kept per shard, chosen by the partition key
  • Pick a well-spread partition key
Exam tip

Many consumers, replayable, real-time: Kinesis Data Streams. Unknown traffic: on-demand mode.

Amazon Data Firehose and Managed Service for Apache Flink Old name

Service What it does Use it for
Amazon Data Firehose (formerly Kinesis Data Firehose) A fully managed delivery service; buffers by size or time; can transform with Lambda and convert to Parquet or ORC Loading streams into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, Splunk, Iceberg tables or HTTP endpoints with no code
Managed Service for Apache Flink (formerly Kinesis Data Analytics) Runs Apache Flink in Java, Scala, Python or SQL Real-time analytics, windowing, streaming ETL
Exam tip

Load a stream into S3 with no servers: Firehose. Compute on the stream: Managed Flink.

A Streaming Architecture

  • Producers write to Kinesis Data Streams
  • Flink computes live metrics from the stream
  • Firehose delivers the raw events to S3 as Parquet
  • Athena queries the lake and Quick shows dashboards

Exam tip

One stream, many uses: real-time processing and durable storage in parallel.

Amazon MSK and Kinesis Video Streams

Service What it is Choose it when
Amazon MSK Managed Apache Kafka: provisioned clusters or MSK Serverless; MSK Connect moves data in and out You already use Kafka and want open-source compatibility
Kinesis Data Streams AWS-native streaming with shards You want AWS integration and simple operations
Kinesis Video Streams Streams live video and time-serialized data from devices for analytics and playback Cameras and sensors
  • Brokers run in each AZ; MSK replaces failed brokers automatically
Exam tip

Existing Kafka applications: MSK. Video from devices: Kinesis Video Streams.

AWS Glue: Catalog, Crawlers and ETL

  • Serverless data integration: discover, prepare, move and integrate data
  • The Data Catalog is a central metadata store that Athena, EMR and Redshift Spectrum read
  • Crawlers infer schemas and fill the catalog automatically
  • ETL jobs run on Apache Spark, built visually in Glue Studio or in code; run on a schedule, on demand or on an event
  • DataBrew cleans data without code
  • Typical transform: CSV to Parquet
Exam tip

Catalog, crawl and transform without servers: AWS Glue. Convert CSV to Parquet: a Glue job.

Building a Data Lake

  • S3 holds raw and curated data; Glue catalogs and transforms it
  • Lake Formation adds central permissions over the catalog and data
  • Athena, EMR, Redshift Spectrum and Quick read the same lake
  • Partition by date and use columnar formats for speed and cost

Exam tip

Many tools, one lake: S3 data, Glue catalog, Lake Formation permissions.

Securing a Data Lake with Lake Formation

  • Lake Formation centrally governs, secures and shares data lake data on S3 and its Glue Data Catalog metadata
  • Its permissions add to IAM, with grant and revoke like a database
  • Control access at the database, table, column, row and cell level; Athena, Redshift Spectrum, EMR, Glue and Quick respect it
  • LF-Tags manage thousands of permissions with a few tags
  • Cross-account sharing; hybrid access mode adopts it step by step
  • CloudTrail audits access; encrypt S3 with KMS; secure ingestion endpoints with IAM, TLS and VPC endpoints
Exam tip

Column or row restrictions on a data lake: Lake Formation permissions.

3Querying, transfer services and practice

Querying and Visualizing Data Old name

Service What it does Use it for
Amazon Athena Serverless SQL directly on S3, with no infrastructure Ad hoc queries on the lake
Amazon OpenSearch Service Managed search and analytics engine with dashboards Log analytics, search, real-time monitoring
Amazon EMR Managed Spark and Hadoop clusters Heavy transformations and large analytics
Amazon Quick (formerly QuickSight) Dashboards and business intelligence Visualization for business users
  • Cut Athena cost and time: Parquet or ORC, partitions, compression, sensible file sizes
Exam tip

SQL on S3 with no servers: Athena. Charts for managers: Quick.

Data Transfer and Integration Services [Verify live]

Service What it does
AWS DataSync Online transfer from NFS, SMB, HDFS or object storage to S3, EFS or FSx; scheduled, encrypted, integrity-checked
Storage Gateway Hybrid access to cloud storage from on premises (module 6)
Amazon AppFlow No-code flows between SaaS apps and AWS, on demand, on a schedule or on an event
AWS Data Exchange Find and subscribe to third-party data sets
Snow Family, Transfer Family Offline and file-protocol transfers (module 11)
  • As of 5 November 2026: AWS Data Pipeline is in maintenance mode and closed to new customers; use Glue or Step Functions
Exam tip

On-premises files to S3 over the network: DataSync. SaaS to AWS with no code: AppFlow.

Choosing Ingestion and Analytics Services

Need Choice
Real-time, many consumers, replay Kinesis Data Streams
Load a stream into S3 or Redshift with no code Amazon Data Firehose
Compute on a stream Managed Service for Apache Flink
Kafka applications Amazon MSK
Catalog and transform AWS Glue
SQL on S3 Amazon Athena
Column and row security Lake Formation
Dashboards Amazon Quick
Bulk files from on premises AWS DataSync
Exam tip

Name the stage: ingest, transform, secure, query or show.

What the Exam Asks: Ingestion and Transformation

  • Which ingestion service for the speed, size and consumers
  • Which transformation: Glue, Firehose, Flink or EMR
  • Which format and layout: Parquet, partitions, compression
  • Which security control: Lake Formation, IAM, VPC endpoints, KMS
  • Which transfer service: DataSync, AppFlow, Snow or Data Exchange
Exam tip

Underline seconds, hours, SQL, Kafka, SaaS and restricted columns.

Design Check: Lantern and Loom Learns from Its Data

Requirement Design
Clickstream, several teams, replay Kinesis Data Streams
Raw events to S3 as Parquet with no consumer code Data Firehose with format conversion
Nightly CSV exports made fast to query Glue job to Parquet, partitioned by date
Analysts want SQL on S3 Amazon Athena over the Glue Data Catalog
Customer columns restricted Lake Formation column-level permissions
CRM data into the lake Amazon AppFlow
Warehouse NAS files to S3 AWS DataSync
Dashboards Amazon Quick
  • Cover the right column, answer each row yourself, then compare

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer; some ask for two)

S1Lantern and Loom's site produces thousands of clickstream events per second. Several teams must read the same events independently in real time, and one team may need to re-read the last few hours. Which service fits?

  • AAn Amazon SQS standard queue
  • BAmazon Data Firehose delivering to S3
  • CAmazon Kinesis Data Streams
  • DAWS AppFlow
Show the answer

Answer: C. Kinesis Data Streams holds records in shards, supports multiple independent consumers, and lets them read recent data again. A queue gives each message to one consumer, Firehose only delivers to a destination, and AppFlow moves SaaS data.

S2Clickstream events must land in Amazon S3 as Parquet files within minutes, and the team does not want to write or run any consumer code. Which solution fits?

  • AAmazon Data Firehose with format conversion turned on
  • BAn EC2 fleet that polls the stream and writes the files itself
  • CKinesis Data Streams with a custom consumer application written by the team
  • DAWS DataSync from the web servers
Show the answer

Answer: A. Firehose is a fully managed delivery service that buffers records, can convert them to Parquet or ORC, and writes them to S3 without code. A polling fleet or a custom consumer needs code and servers, and DataSync copies files.

S3Analysts query large CSV files in Amazon S3 with Athena, and the queries are slow and costly. Which change helps most?

  • ASpread the files across additional S3 buckets
  • BTurn on S3 Transfer Acceleration
  • CCompress all the CSV data into one large gzip file in the bucket
  • DConvert the data to Parquet and partition it by date
Show the answer

Answer: D. Columnar formats such as Parquet and partitioning let Athena read less data, which speeds queries and lowers cost. More buckets and Transfer Acceleration do not reduce the data scanned, and one large gzip file cannot be split for parallel reads.

S4Which TWO statements about AWS Lake Formation are correct? (Select TWO.)

  • AIt can restrict access at the column, row and cell level
  • BIts permissions remove the need to encrypt the data in S3
  • CLF-Tags let a few tags control access to many databases, tables and columns
  • DIt stores the data itself instead of using S3
  • EIt works only inside a single AWS account
Show the answer

Answer: A, C. Lake Formation adds fine-grained permissions to the Glue Data Catalog and S3 data, and LF-Tags scale those permissions. Data stays in S3 and should still be encrypted, and Lake Formation supports cross-account sharing.

S5Lantern and Loom must copy 40 terabytes of warehouse files from an on-premises NFS server to Amazon S3 over the network, on a schedule, with encryption and integrity checks. Which service should it use?

  • AAmazon Kinesis Data Streams
  • BAWS DataSync, scheduled with built-in verification
  • CAmazon AppFlow
  • DAmazon MSK
Show the answer

Answer: B. DataSync automates online transfers from NFS and SMB sources to S3, with scheduling, encryption and data integrity validation. Kinesis and MSK are for streams, and AppFlow moves SaaS data.

5Quick Reference Card
